title: What Is This?
tagline: Point at things, ask whose they are, say "too" and say "it's not".
hook: Hana's grandmother runs a tiny café, and every shelf is full of things you don't know the names of yet. Time to point, ask and politely disagree.
goals: Choose between これ, それ and あれ by distance
Say "also" with も and ask "whose?" with だれの
Deny something politely with じゃないです

points.title: これ・それ・あれ / この・その・あの
points.gist: Choose by distance: near me, near you, far from both.
explain: Japanese points in three steps. こ- is near the speaker, そ- is near the listener, あ- is far from both. The same trick builds ここ / そこ / あそこ for places.
これ, それ, あれ stand alone: "this one". この, その, あの must sit in front of a noun: この かさ (this umbrella).

examples.ja: その|かさは|だれのですか。

points.tip: When you point at something near the listener, switch to そ-: it's "theirs" territory.
points.watch: これ can't be followed directly by a noun. これ ケーキ is wrong; use この ケーキ.

points.title: 〜も
explain: も takes the place of は (or を, が) to say "also". It keeps the sentence shape but adds "too".
Never write はも. も already does the topic job.

examples.en: Is that a cake as well?

examples.ja: コーヒーも|おちゃも|あります。
examples.en: There is coffee and also tea.

points.tip: Use も twice to mean "both": コーヒーも ケーキも すきです.
points.watch: も replaces は, it doesn't stack with it.

points.title: 〜じゃないです
points.formula: A は B じゃないです
explain: To say "is not" swap です for じゃないです. A slightly more careful version is じゃありません.
To answer a yes/no question negatively, start with いいえ and then repeat what's true.

examples.ja: これは|かさじゃないです。
いいえ、|わたしのじゃありません。
レオさんは|先生じゃないです。

points.tip: じゃ is the friendly spoken form of では. You will hear both.
points.watch: Don't say いいえ、です. After いいえ, change the sentence to the negative.

points.title: だれの / 〜の (whose)
points.formula: だれの + noun / A の
points.gist: Whose? / the one belonging to A.
explain: Put の after a name and you get a possessive. だれの is the question form: "whose?".
If the noun is obvious, you can skip it and end with の: それは わたしの です.

examples.ja: それは|ハナさんのです。

points.tip: In English you need the noun again ("mine" is a different word). In Japanese you just keep の.
points.watch: Don't add さん to yourself: わたしの, never わたしさんの.

drills.q: The cake is right next to YOU. Which word do you use?

drills.ja: ＿ かさは だれのですか。 (the umbrella near the listener)
drills.why: A noun follows, so use その, not それ.
も replaces は to say "also".

options: わたしはも 学生です。
わたしも 学生です。
コーヒーも すきです。
それも ケーキです。
drills.why: も replaces は; you can't use them together.

drills.ja: これは かさ＿ないです。
drills.why: じゃないです is the negative of です.

drills.q: "Is this yours?" You say it isn't. Which is correct?
options: いいえ、わたしのじゃないです。
はい、わたしのじゃないです。
いいえ、わたしの か。

drills.ja: これは ＿のですか。 (Whose is this?)

Type the reading of 財布 (wallet) in hiragana.

drills.q: How do you ask the price?
